reflections.title: Seeking the Lord in Prayer

reflect.text: Jeremiah warned that disaster was coming because the leaders had become foolish and failed to seek the Lord. When shepherds do not pray and ask for God's guidance, their flock ends up scattered. F. B. Meyer reminds us that when God's work weakens or struggles, a lack of prayer is very often the reason. It is good for each of us to search our hearts and see if our own prayerlessness is holding back God's blessing.

The good news is that the opposite is also true: when we seek the Lord, our spiritual work will prosper. True prayer is not wasted time; it is real labor. As Meyer points out, quiet prayer behind closed doors can accomplish just as much good as being busy with outward activity in the world. Some of the greatest work ever done has been accomplished through simple prayer.

When we pray, we do not come because of our own goodness. We approach God only through Jesus and His cross. We should pray for God's glory, put away any sin that blocks His blessing, and wait patiently for Him to answer. When we seek the Lord instead of trusting our own wisdom, He protects and guides His people.

questions: In what areas of your life are you relying on your own strength instead of seeking God in prayer?
How can you make more time this week to quietly pray for others?
reflections.prayer: Lord, forgive us for the times we try to walk in our own wisdom without seeking You. Teach us to labor faithfully in prayer, trusting only in what Christ has done for us. Help us to turn away from sin, live for Your glory, and wait patiently on You. Amen.
